why: Pure stubbornness. No Chaos and no complex mechanics. Build a wall of stone and crush everything that comes at it.
tip: Let the enemy come to you and grind them down. Armour-piercing artillery and Ironbreakers win most fights.
keyMechanic: Grudge Book – every wrong done to the Dwarfs is recorded and must be avenged.

why: The quintessential all-rounder. Cavalry infantry artillery and magic – everything is available. Ideal for getting back into the game.
tip: Unite the Elector Counts early – the political mechanic is simple and rewarding.
keyMechanic: Elector Counts – provincial lords must be diplomatically united or subjugated.

why: Brain-off aggression. Charge forward kill everything and keep the Waaagh! rolling.
tip: Never lose momentum – Greenskin armies that stop fighting start squabbling. Black Orcs anchor any line.
keyMechanic: Waaagh! – fighting builds Waaagh! until a free army spawns to follow your lord.

why: Reworked in Update 9.0. Armies are raised through Necromancy instead of recruited and corpses and blood are now currencies. Atmospheric and still forgiving.
tip: Fight where the dead pile up – corpses fuel your armies. Spend blood to awaken vampire lords from their tombs.
keyMechanic: Necromancy and Bloodlines (Update 9.0) – raise units from corpses and awaken vampire lords with blood for bloodline bonuses.

why: The grand finale. Mortal champions of the Dark Gods marching as a global threat. Update 9.0 lets Archaon subjugate the other Chaos lords.
tip: Commit to one Chaos God per lord – trying to please all of them at once spreads you thin.
keyMechanic: Marks of Chaos – lords and units take the mark of a Chaos God for powerful bonuses and unique units.

why: A horde faction that lives to ruin civilisation. No settlements to manage – just constant aggressive movement. Unique and atmospheric.
tip: Never stop moving. Ambush stance is your greatest weapon – use it every turn you can and raze what you cannot hold.
keyMechanic: Herdstones and Dread – ruin enemy lands to earn Dread and build Herdstones that power your warherds.

why: Living around Athel Loren the Wood Elves run on Amber instead of conquest. Elite troops and a very different strategic approach.
tip: Amber is everything – prioritise it above all else and don't over-expand outside the forest early on.
keyMechanic: Amber Economy – Amber unlocks the strongest Wood Elf units buildings and technologies.

why: Pure cavalry fantasy. Line up your knights and smash through everything with one of the most satisfying charges in the game.
tip: Lead with Knights of the Realm and keep peasant bowmen behind. Fight honourably – Chivalry unlocks your strongest units.
keyMechanic: Chivalry – heroic acts earn Chivalry which unlocks Grail units and powerful bonuses.

why: Fast aggressive raiding with powerful monsters. No complex economy – just raid loot and conquer.
tip: Raid every coastal settlement you can early on – income comes from pillaging not from holding territory.
keyMechanic: Monster Hunting – hunt legendary monsters across the map to unlock powerful Regiments of Renown.

why: Expensive but powerful troops and an introduction to Elven court politics.
tip: Avoid early over-expansion – gather gold research technologies and then strike with elite units.
keyMechanic: Intrigue at the Court – spend Influence to manipulate diplomacy between other factions.

why: Cruel elite and fast. Slaves fuel the economy and Black Arks give every Dark Elf faction a mobile fortress at sea.
tip: Keep fighting to keep slaves flowing and use Black Arks to strike where the enemy is weakest.
keyMechanic: Black Arks and Slaves – floating fortresses that recruit at sea and captives that power your cities.

why: Dinosaurs as an army. Powerful frontline monsters and no complicated resource management.
tip: Carnosaurs and Stegadons create an unstoppable frontline. Connect your temple-cities as you expand.
keyMechanic: Geomantic Web – connect temple-cities for powerful campaign bonuses.

why: Massive swarm armies with insane technology. Medium learning curve but enormous fun factor.
tip: Keep food up or the clan falls apart. Betray everyone – that is Skaven tradition.
keyMechanic: Under-Empire – hidden nests beneath enemy cities that can be detonated or expanded for income.

why: Undead armies with zero upkeep and powerful constructs. Unit caps and Canopic Jars replace the normal economy for elite units.
tip: Prioritise the Mortuary Cult early. Canopic Jars for Tomb Scorpions and Sphinxes win campaigns.
keyMechanic: Mortuary Cult – spend Canopic Jars to craft magic items and legendary constructs outside normal recruitment.

why: Undead pirates with a unique Infamy system and a powerful naval presence.
tip: Coastal raids generate Infamy which unlocks the most powerful units. Prioritise ships and coastal settlements.
keyMechanic: Infamy – raiding and winning battles builds Infamy for recruiting Pirate Captains and campaign bonuses.

why: Ice magic and a defensive frontier war against Chaos. Demanding but deeply satisfying.
tip: Lean on Frost Maidens and Ice Guard early. Hold the line before trying to expand north.
keyMechanic: Ice Court and Supporters – train ice witches and win the backing of the Orthodoxy or the Tzarina for bonuses.

why: Celestial dragons and an empire that balances harmony and trade. Feels fresh compared to WH1 and WH2.
tip: Keep Yin and Yang in balance and keep caravans running on the Ivory Road for steady income.
keyMechanic: Harmony – too much Yin or Yang incurs penalties while balance grants powerful bonuses.

why: Pure aggression turned into a resource. Every battle and razed city feeds the Blood God.
tip: Never end a turn without fighting. Raze what you cannot use – skulls are worth more than cities.
keyMechanic: Skull Throne – battles and razing collect skulls which are offered for powerful empire-wide boons.

why: Slow methodical corruption. Spread disease across the map and let attrition work before your armies arrive.
tip: Spread plagues into enemy territory before moving your armies. Nurgle armies are slow but nearly impossible to kill.
keyMechanic: Plagues – mix symptoms into plagues and spread them through armies agents and settlements.

why: The most magic-focused faction in the game. Manipulate other factions instead of fighting every war yourself.
tip: Spend Grimoires on Changing of the Ways to set your enemies against each other before you strike.
keyMechanic: Changing of the Ways – spend Grimoires to rewrite diplomacy move armies and twist other factions' fates.

why: The fastest armies in the game and a campaign built around seducing rivals into serving you.
tip: Seduce rather than destroy – a vassal fighting for you is worth more than a dead enemy. Speed is your greatest weapon.
keyMechanic: Seductive Influence – spread Slaaneshi influence to turn enemy factions and units into your servants.

why: Small elite armies that punch far above their weight and hire themselves out for gold.
tip: Take contracts early for gold and keep your armies fed – hungry Ogres fight badly.
keyMechanic: Contracts and Meat – take paid contracts from other factions and keep Meat flowing to fuel your armies.

why: Complex economic system built on slave labour and industry. One of the deepest campaign loops in the game.
tip: Labour is the engine – without it nothing works. Raid and capture from the very start.
keyMechanic: Labour Economy – captured labour drives the factories that make your armour artillery and daemonic engines.

why: Build your Daemon Prince from scratch choosing gifts from all four Chaos Gods. Every campaign is different.
tip: Plan your path before starting. Mixing too many gods weakens you – commit to one or two.
keyMechanic: Daemonic Gifts – earn Glory with the Chaos Gods to unlock their daemons and gifts that reshape your prince.

why: The Great Necromancer himself. Commands Tomb Kings Vampire Counts and Vampire Coast units in one army. Immortal Empires only.
tip: Build your first Necropolis in a central major settlement surrounded by provinces you hold or plan to take.
keyMechanic: Black Pyramid – spend Empowered Sigils to upgrade the Pyramid and Necromantic Energy to raise armies instantly.
